nodes.description: Public string state variable storing the current riddle/question text.
Address state variable acting as the owner/administrator of the game; used for access control in StopGame, NewQuestion and newQuestioner.
Bytes32 state variable holding the keccak256 hash of the expected answer.
External payable function that verifies the answer hash and value > 3 ether, then transfers the whole contract balance to msg.sender.
Public payable initializer that sets responseHash, question and questionSender only when responseHash is still zero.
Public payable function restricted to questionSender that drains the entire contract balance to msg.sender.
Public payable function allowing questionSender to replace the question and responseHash.
Public function allowing questionSender to transfer ownership to a new address.
Payable fallback function that accepts plain ether transfers.
Caller-controlled address used for authorization checks and as ether transfer recipient.
Origin address used in Try's require(msg.sender == tx.origin) authorization check.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Try: external ETH send to an untrusted address.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame: external ETH send to an untrusted address.
User-supplied answer string parameter of Try, hashed and compared against responseHash.
Question string parameter of set_game written to the question state variable.
Answer string parameter of set_game hashed into responseHash.
New question string parameter of NewQuestion written to the question state variable.
New answer hash parameter of NewQuestion written to responseHash.
New owner address parameter of newQuestioner written into questionSender.

edges.reason: Try's authorization uses the untrusted caller address msg.sender in require(msg.sender == tx.origin).
Try relies on tx.origin as an authorization factor, enabling phishing-based bypass of the access check.
Try reads responseHash to compare it against keccak256(_response).
The _response parameter is hashed inside Try before the comparison.
keccak256(_response) is compared with the stored responseHash value.
When the hash check and msg.value > 3 ether condition hold, Try executes the external transfer.
The untrusted msg.sender is the recipient of the balance transfer, allowing interaction with attacker-controlled code.
transfer to msg.sender may execute code in the recipient contract, which can re-enter the payable fallback.
set_game writes keccak256(_response) into responseHash.
set_game writes _question into the question state variable.
set_game assigns msg.sender to questionSender, establishing the privileged owner.
Anyone can call set_game while responseHash is zero and claim ownership via msg.sender.
The _question parameter flows into the question state variable inside set_game.
The _response parameter is hashed inside set_game and stored.
StopGame's require(msg.sender == questionSender) authorizes based on the questionSender state variable.
StopGame checks the untrusted caller msg.sender against the stored owner address.
StopGame performs an external balance transfer to the owner once the access check passes.
msg.sender receives the full contract balance in StopGame, enabling reentrant interaction.
The transfer to msg.sender can trigger the recipient's fallback and re-enter the contract.
NewQuestion gates state changes on msg.sender == questionSender.
NewQuestion compares the untrusted caller against the owner before updating state.
NewQuestion overwrites the question state variable.
NewQuestion overwrites responseHash with the supplied bytes32 value.
The _question parameter is written to the question state variable.
The _responseHash parameter is written to the responseHash state variable.
newQuestioner checks msg.sender == questionSender and reassigns questionSender.
The untrusted caller msg.sender is compared against the owner in newQuestioner.
newQuestioner transfers ownership by writing the new address into questionSender.
The newAddress parameter becomes the new questionSender value.

normalization_plan.reason: The _response parameter is only used inside Try for hashing and comparison; it carries no standalone semantic value.
The _question parameter is only consumed by set_game to initialize the question state variable.
The _response parameter is only hashed and stored by set_game during initialization.
The _question parameter is only assigned to the question state variable inside NewQuestion.
The _responseHash parameter is only assigned to the responseHash state variable inside NewQuestion.
The newAddress parameter is only used by newQuestioner to update the owner address.
